absent: Hardware effects of chip callbacks for masking, acknowledgment, type programming, bus synchronization, and wakeup handling.
Full lifecycles for activation, startup, shutdown, hierarchical domains, suspend, resume, and power managed rearming.
Creation, waking, oneshot completion, and teardown of threaded handlers including nested and secondary threads.
Affinity selection, balancing, migration, managed shutdown, and effective mask computation beyond display.
Resend, replay, pending, polling, autodetection, and spurious disable decisions beyond injection preconditions.
Complete record layouts and ownership for descriptors, data, chips, actions, and domains beyond referenced fields.
Proc structure, sparse number allocation, and slow bus synchronization beyond removal and enumeration guards.

findings.text: Requesting a threaded line validates the caller supplied line number and option combination before creating handler state. Disconnected lines, missing descriptors, lines that forbid requests, and per CPU device identifier lines are rejected. Shared lines require a caller token and forbid auto disable suppression, conditional suspend requires sharing and forbids no suspend, primary handling defaults when only threaded handling is supplied, allocation failure and power acquisition failure abort, and setup failure releases power and memory.

Releasing a line removes the handler record that matches the caller token and returns its name, or reports absence when no match exists. The operation rejects missing descriptors and per CPU device identifier lines, protects lookup and unlink with request and bus guards, updates power bookkeeping, shuts down and later deactivates the line only when the final handler leaves, waits for quiescence before stopping threads and releasing resources, and balances power and module references.

Disabling and enabling lines is nestable through a depth counter. The first disable transition actuates hardware and then waits for completion, while nested disables only adjust depth. A no sync variant performs only the guarded depth update and reports invalid lines, and enabling verifies that chip state exists before delegating to shared re enable logic.

Synchronization provides a quiescent view of a line by waiting for redirect work, hard handling, and threaded handling to finish. The hard wait polls an in progress marker, rechecks under lock, optionally consults chip active state when supported, and repeats until clear. The outer wait then blocks until the active thread count reaches zero. Public lookup tolerates missing descriptors, and redirect handling has active and empty build variants.

Injection attempts to raise a line by number for diagnostics. A hardware pending state attempt is tried first and success returns immediately. When unsupported, the implementation guards the descriptor and bus, requires that the line is not marked for non maskable handling and that its data is activated, then attempts delivery through the resend path and reports its outcome, otherwise reporting invalid argument.

Per line debug display summarizes handler identity, device naming, status and internal state words with decoded bit names, disable and wake depths, data state with decoded names, node placement, affinity masks, and hierarchical domain and chip information including parent links. Bit decoding prints only names whose mask overlaps current state. Chip display tolerates absence, domain display tolerates missing names and operations, hierarchy recursion ends at the top, and mask display has reporting and empty build variants. Collection holds the descriptor lock.

Per line debug files bind open to the summary display and accept bounded writes. Open associates the descriptor with sequential output. Write copies a small user buffer, fails on copy fault, invokes interrupt injection when the buffer carries the trigger keyword and propagates injection errors, otherwise succeeds without effect while reporting the requested length.

Debug filesystem setup publishes interrupt and domain views and manages their lifetime. Initialization creates top level and per line and domain directories, a default domain view, numbered per line files for active lines under a sparse guard, and per domain files under a mutex. Per line creation skips when directories or descriptors are missing or a file already exists, domain file creation skips when names or directories are missing, device name caching duplicates the device string, and removal deletes the file and frees the cached name. Empty variants exist when debug support is disabled, and file handling maps open and write to debug helpers with sequential read and seek and single release.

Bit decoding uses a small record pairing a numeric mask with a human readable name, plus a helper that builds such records by stringifying the mask expression. A header guard macro protects the debug header from repeated inclusion.
Device managed interrupt state is a compact record holding a line number together with the caller token supplied at request time.

Device managed requesting allocates bookkeeping, defaults an absent name from the device, requests the line through the threaded path, and on success records the line and token and attaches the bookkeeping, while allocation failure aborts and request failure discards bookkeeping and reports a detailed error. Matching compares both line and token, and release frees the line using the stored values.

Power and proc bookkeeping for handler removal has active and empty build variants. The active power helper decrements total and suspend related depths according to force resume and suspend option flags, while the empty variant does nothing. The active proc helper removes the handler directory, while the empty variant does nothing.

Interrupt teardown and inspection follow strict guard ordering. Handler removal acquires the request mutex, then the chip bus guard, then the descriptor spinlock, drops the bus guard before waiting for quiescence to avoid deadlock with threaded completion, and reacquires it for resource release. Debug display holds the descriptor lock during collection, hard quiescence rechecks under lock, domain enumeration holds a mutex, active line enumeration holds a sparse guard, and bus operations invoke chip callbacks only when implemented.

Disable depth starts at zero, increments on each disable with hardware actuation only on the first step, and is undone by enabling. Synchronization moves from redirect quiescence to hard quiescence with polling plus locked recheck and optional chip query looping until clear, then to thread quiescence waiting for the active count to reach zero.

Several misuse paths warn or fail safely. Releasing from interrupt context warns, releasing an unknown token warns and yields no result, enabling before setup warns about missing chip state, unexpected affinity notification or hint state warns, shared debug paths may invoke handlers outside normal delivery, and debug writes fail cleanly on user copy faults while trigger failures propagate injection errors.

Debug presentation uses stable names and access modes. Top areas are named irq and irqs and domains, per line files carry decimal line numbers with mode 0644, domain views include a default entry with mode 0444, and writes carrying trigger request injection.

Diagnostic logging of descriptors is rate limited and best effort. When the limiter allows, it reports line identity, descriptor address, depth and counting fields, handler and chip addresses with symbolic form, action presence with handler detail when present, and selected status helpers, otherwise emitting nothing.
